title: Checks Studio translation review consolidation

functional.description: Keep the left Steps panel as the sole default location for the complete ordered natural-language checklist, including its existing editing, validation, reordering, and run-state affordances.
functional.rationale: One canonical authoring surface removes duplicate checklist scanning.

functional.description: Replace the always-expanded duplicate step list in the Control Tower with a compact translation/readiness summary that communicates compile state, readiness or blocker, candidate or confirmed revision identity when applicable, diagnostic attention count, and the next valid action.
functional.rationale: Daily users need a decision and next action, not a second checklist.

functional.description: Offer an explicit Review translation details disclosure. Only on request, it provides ordered index-aligned source-to-artifact evidence, server-derived action/target/assertion summaries, per-step diagnostics, and opt-in code. Source text is a secondary cross-reference, never a second editable checklist.
functional.rationale: The exact-revision safety review remains available without dominating routine operation.

functional.description: In NEEDS_REVISION, surface the number of affected steps and a concise action to edit them; enable navigation and focus to the first affected source row in the left Steps panel. Keep detailed diagnostics available through the explicit review disclosure.
functional.rationale: Exceptions must direct users to corrective work rather than make them scan successful rows.

functional.description: Preserve explicit, exact-revision confirmation. It is enabled only for AWAITING_CONFIRMATION with a candidate and available artifact hash; no automatic confirmation, gate bypass, or semantic change to stale/conflict/in-flight handling is allowed.
functional.rationale: The confirmation control is the product's human safety control point.

functional.description: Render distinct compact states for COMPILING, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, READY, NEEDS_REVISION, and STALE. Each explains what is true, what the user may do, and what is blocked; READY makes the confirmed runnable revision available without repeating steps.
functional.rationale: Operational users need clear state-specific decisions.

functional.description: Keep review/readiness before Logs, Code, and Proof in the Control Tower, using established MUI visual language and a single label set for Translation, Review details, and confirmation.
functional.rationale: The control should be discoverable without displacing execution evidence.

nonFunctional.description: A full authored step string appears no more than once in the default Studio viewport; compact review is outcome-first and does not render a second source checklist.
nonFunctional.metric: Automated component test asserts no repeated source rows before Review translation details is activated.

nonFunctional.description: Preserve named review regions, polite state announcements, keyboard-operable disclosure, focus restoration, visible non-colour state indicators, and diagnostic-to-step associations.
nonFunctional.metric: Existing accessibility coverage remains passing; new disclosure and focus behavior are covered by automated tests.

nonFunctional.description: Compact review is available from the existing review state and opening/closing details introduces neither duplicate polling nor additional request lifecycle.
nonFunctional.metric: No new API operation or polling schedule; existing compile-poll tests continue to pass.

nonFunctional.description: Translation summaries and code remain read-only projections of the server candidate artifact; secret values are never surfaced.
nonFunctional.metric: No client-side parsing/generation path is added; existing artifact/source safety tests remain passing.

nonFunctional.description: At narrow widths controls remain usable without horizontal overflow and authoring precedes review/action in reading order.
nonFunctional.metric: Responsive component/E2E coverage verifies usable controls at the project breakpoint.

constraints.description: test.steps remains the server draft source of truth; summaries and code may only derive from currentCandidateArtifact.
constraints.impact: The UI may not reconstruct translated meaning from authored English.

constraints.description: Positional alignment defects among steps, diagnostics, and artifact entries must remain visible rather than silently repaired.
constraints.impact: The detail view must retain the current honest defect treatment.

constraints.description: CompileReviewPanel remains the sole owner of compile polling, confirmation, and recompile transactions.
constraints.impact: No duplicated transaction logic or request paths may be introduced.

constraints.description: The implementation is front-end UX work; compiler semantics, API contracts, editor behavior, and execution Logs/Code/Proof capability are out of scope.
constraints.impact: The change must not expand into backend or workflow redesign.

assumptions.description: An inline disclosure beneath the compact review state is the preferred detail pattern because it retains the existing focus and poll ownership.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A product decision for a drawer or modal changes interaction and focus requirements.

assumptions.description: Aggregate status plus exception-first detail is preferable to always displaying every semantic operation for daily operations users.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Audit users may need a denser default review summary.

flow: Steps remain the canonical authoring view
Control Tower presents a compact translation state
User reads next action or opens Review translation details
Exact candidate may be confirmed only when eligible

states.error: NEEDS_REVISION directs focus to affected steps
states.empty: No candidate evidence is disclosed honestly

flow: User reads indexed artifact-derived evidence and optional code
User closes details and focus returns to the disclosure control

states.error: Alignment and artifact absence are explicitly surfaced
states.empty: No candidate is never represented as translated

edgeCases.scenario: Candidate artifact is absent or cannot be summarized
edgeCases.handling: Retain explicit unavailable wording; do not infer from English.

edgeCases.scenario: Diagnostics/artifact entries do not align with authored steps
edgeCases.handling: Show existing alignment defect rather than reordering or padding.

edgeCases.scenario: Candidate becomes stale or confirmation conflicts
edgeCases.handling: Retain current recompile/re-read and in-flight protections.

terminology.definition: The canonical natural-language checklist authored by the user.
The server-produced candidate artifact and its validated interpretation of a draft.
Intentional progressive disclosure of indexed artifact evidence, diagnostics, and optional code.

acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: With a candidate awaiting confirmation, initial review is compact and shows translation/readiness state, revision identity, translated-step count, and diagnostic attention count without rendering all authored steps.

AC-2: Mouse and keyboard users can open and close Review translation details; the opened view contains indexed source cross-references, server-derived summaries, diagnostics, and opt-in code without refetching.
AC-3: NEEDS_REVISION names the affected-step count, gives actionable edit guidance, and navigates/focuses the first affected source row; it never shows a confirmable candidate.
AC-4: COMPILING, READY, and STALE remain compact and expose only state-appropriate guidance and controls; STALE exposes recompile and READY identifies the confirmed runnable revision.
AC-5: Confirmation behavior is unchanged: only AWAITING_CONFIRMATION with candidate and available hash enables it; one request may be in flight and conflict/reconfirmation handling remains intact.
AC-6: Artifact absence, malformed/unrecognized artifact data, and alignment mismatches are truthfully disclosed without guessing translated meaning.
AC-7: Screen-reader and keyboard users can find state, operate detail disclosure, return focus to its trigger, and use confirmation/recompile; state/severity is not color-only.
AC-8: Desktop retains complementary Steps and Control Tower panels; narrow layouts preserve authoring before review/action and leave controls usable.
